rows.intent: User only describes intent or picks an option; the system picks the skill and runs the underlying CLI on the user's behalf.

outputs.name: routedSkill + confidence
outputs.shape: JSON envelope with ok / data / warnings / nextActions

invariants: The CLI verb is never shown to the user as a required input
The user only ever picks an option or describes intent in natural language
The LLM, not the user, executes the underlying CLI command
forbiddenChanges: Adding a CLI verb as a required argument to the user-facing surface
Pushing the user toward hand-authoring a JSON manifest or skill name

rows.intent: A user requirement moves through goal bind, RD, implementation, QA, and final review; every hard gate stops the slice on failure.

outputs.name: stage transition log + verdict
outputs.shape: JSON envelope with stage + state + verdict

invariants: Every hard gate (audit / RD / QA / final-review) is enforced; a failure transitions state back to the prior role
The user never hand-authors a SKILL.md, manifest, or gate JSON to keep the lifecycle moving
The pipeline state machine advances only when each role's verdict is recorded
forbiddenChanges: Allowing a slice to bypass a hard gate by skipping the verdict log
Forcing the user to type a CLI verb (e.g. peaks workflow advance) to move the slice

rows.intent: A reproducible failure mode is captured as a regression test, fixed, and proven not to break adjacent capabilities.

outputs.name: regression-test patch + adjacent-test proof
outputs.shape: JSON envelope with new test + green adjacent suite

invariants: Every regression fix lands with a vitest/integration test that fails on the unfixed code path
Adjacent capabilities (the rid-005 closure set) remain green after the fix
No silent-catch or fake-green pattern is reintroduced in src/services/**
forbiddenChanges: Marking a regression fixed without a test that fails on the unfixed code
Using --exclude or .skip to make the suite green

rows.intent: A user-approved goal (intent, scope, non-goals, success criteria, red lines) exists before implementation and is not silently rewritten.
invariants: Autonomous LLM work never proceeds on a partial audit; IncompleteAuditError halts the slice
The audit covers exactly six dimensions: correctness, completeness, scope, risks, alternatives, constraints
The goal is the only contract that downstream RD / QA read from; it is never silently rewritten
forbiddenChanges: Removing any of the six required audit dimensions from auditGoal()
Allowing RD to start without an accepted goal artifact

rows.intent: Before any slice exits, all four dimensions (functional / problem / no-new / intact) are evidenced; ambiguous items surface to the user.
invariants: Every final review contains exactly four dimensions: functional-completeness, problem-resolution, no-new-bugs, existing-functionality-intact
Ambiguous verdicts (inconclusive / low-confidence) surface to the user, never auto-pass
The review command exits non-zero when any dimension lacks evidence
forbiddenChanges: Allowing a slice to exit on three of four dimensions
Replacing the evidence list with a free-form LLM string

rows.intent: After compaction, session exit, or restart, the system locates the deepest completed gate and offers a resume option.

outputs.name: resume plan / deepest-completed gate
outputs.shape: JSON envelope with resume-from stage and nextActions

invariants: The resume option always identifies the deepest completed gate (audit / RD / QA / final-review)
Resume never silently re-runs an already-passed gate
The user only picks from a list of resume options; the CLI verb is run by the LLM
forbiddenChanges: Auto-advancing past a gate on resume without an explicit user choice
Forcing the user to type a CLI verb to resume

rows.intent: The user only says "run tests"; the LLM runs the correct suite and reports results honestly. No fake green.

outputs.name: vitest summary + per-file status
outputs.shape: JSON envelope with pass / fail / skip counts

invariants: vitest 4.1.10 is the only test runner; the suite MUST NOT be locked at 5.x
Per-test fingerprint cache never returns 'passed' for an unverified file (fileMtime + fileSha256 gate)
Test-cache writes never go to source-controlled paths (gitignored under .peaks/_runtime/)
forbiddenChanges: Bumping vitest to 5.x to satisfy a coverage threshold
Skipping tests via describe.skip / it.skip to make the suite green

rows.intent: A successful run is promoted only after gates pass and a regression-skeptic check; replays are gated by anti-drift evaluation.

outputs.name: loop_release + bee_release rows
outputs.shape: crystallized asset envelope with rl-* compliance

invariants: Crystallization requires all gates (audit / RD / QA / final-review) to be in a passing state
Every crystallized release honors the karpathy-engineered red lines defined in .peaks/standards/loop-engineering-guidelines.md
Replays are gated by anti-drift evaluation before any new release row is inserted
forbiddenChanges: Crystallizing an asset when any gate is in a non-passing state
Crystallizing without referencing the loop-engineering-guidelines file

rows.intent: A user describes a procedure; the system generates, validates, and registers a runnable SOP with checkable gates.

inputs.name: procedure description
inputs.shape: free text or cli flag (id, name)

outputs.name: manifest + skill registration
outputs.shape: JSON envelope with initSop / lintSop envelope

invariants: An SOP id must match SOP_ID_PATTERN (lowercase kebab, no dots/slashes) to prevent path traversal
Reserved prefixes (peaks-, peaks) cannot be authored by users
lintSop() runs before registerSop() so the manifest is valid at registration time
forbiddenChanges: Authoring an SOP outside of initSop() that bypasses lintSop()
Bypassing the SOP_ID_PATTERN guard to write to a reserved path

rows.intent: LLM can install, switch, check, and uninstall hooks / statusline / handle; permission gaps escalate honestly, no silent fake success.

outputs.name: settings.json diff + post-install status
outputs.shape: JSON envelope with plan / apply / read result

invariants: planHookInstall() runs before applyHookInstall() so the diff is reviewable
Permission gaps return a structured HOOK_PERMISSION_DENIED, never silently swallowed
The hooks-settings-service is the single source of truth; no parallel writes to ~/.claude/settings.json
forbiddenChanges: Writing to settings.json outside of applyHookInstall()
Returning ok=true when a hook could not be installed

rows.intent: Audit + L3 doctor + convert to OpenSpec change records; failures stop.

outputs.name: openspec change draft + freezing step
outputs.shape: JSON envelope with change-id + freeze envelope

invariants: Every OpenSpec change is generated from a doctor finding or red-line failure, never hallucinated
Doctor checks live under src/services/doctor/doctor-service/checks/ as a code-driven fixed-registry tree
A doctor check failure halts the conversion; partial proposals are rejected
forbiddenChanges: Generating an openspec change without a doctor finding or red-line failure
Re-introducing the legacy monolithic doctor-service.ts

rows.intent: Dispatch / worktree lease / heartbeat / release / GC form a complete lifecycle without conflict or leak.

outputs.name: lease lifecycle log
outputs.shape: JSON envelope with spawn / renew / list / gc / release

invariants: Every spawn writes a lease; every terminal heartbeat fires a release; gc never runs against an in-flight lease
The lease store is a pure-function module; atomic FS writes happen at the CLI command
Auto-release on terminal heartbeat is best-effort but idempotent: duplicate release is a no-op
forbiddenChanges: Spawning a worktree without writing a corresponding lease row
Running gc against a lease whose heartbeat is still active

rows.intent: Draft → edit → tone check → publish → archive moves through the gates.
invariants: Every stage transition (draft → edit → tone-check → publish → archive) is recorded in the workflow state machine
A tone-check or compliance-gate failure halts the lifecycle; partial publish is rejected
The skill does NOT import peaks-code internals; it reuses the Loop Engineering primitives
forbiddenChanges: Skipping the tone-check gate to publish faster
Importing peaks-code domain logic into peaks-content

rows.intent: Triage → classify → reference merged-PRs → fix → commit → PR draft.

outputs.name: per-issue PR description files + submit script
outputs.shape: JSON envelope with PR body files

invariants: Every fix carries an AI-modified declaration in the commit body (RL-3)
Rubric-banned targets (OAuth / secrets / agent-loop / prompt-cache) are refused before any commit
Per-batch commits land on per-batch branches with normalized PR bodies
forbiddenChanges: Fixing issues on a security-critical hot path (auth / secrets / agent loop / prompt cache)
Skipping the AI-modified declaration to ship faster

rows.intent: A change is archived only when its `Capability Mapping` block matches the c8 coverage summary.
invariants: Pre-cond 2 (Coverage Evidence) is enforced: capability rows must be marked 'covered' AND coverage-summary.json must agree
Coverage-summary discovery order is fixed: <projectRoot>/coverage/coverage-summary.json then /openspec/coverage-summary.json
--force compounds with coverageGateBypassed + coverageMismatchBypassed flags; never silent
forbiddenChanges: Allowing archive without a ## Capability Mapping block in proposal.md
Bypassing the c8 cross-check without the explicit bypass flags
